prompt.utterance: My tony style and the applicable technology style disagree on a discretionary coding choice. Which style controls that coding choice?

graderOnly: The conflict the user describes is purely discretionary: neither rule is required for correctness, repository tooling, project instructions, or framework semantics.
The project has no formatter, linter, or other repository-enforced style configuration, and no project instructions about coding style.

The development plan is PROPOSED and awaiting user approval (Active Work.BlockedOn records the approval request), so no implementation is expected in this run; the tony selection is persisted but not yet locked.

all.why: answering a precedence question does not change the explicit tony selection

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
the plan is unapproved, so no implementation may change, and Developer never edits the user-owned style file

the selected tony user style resolves to exactly one file

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 00-project (pre-install): a small stdlib Python inventory CLI (inventory/stock.py, inventory/cli.py) with pytest tests and no formatter/linter config. 10-style: the user's own .standards/user-styles/developer/tony.md with discretionary Python preferences. 20-cycle: Auditor CONTEXT.md, scope (AC-001..AC-003), and technical design for a low-stock report; STATE at DEVELOPING after a FORWARD from ARCHITECTING. 30-plan: Developer plan created with User Style `tony`, User Style Locked `false`, Status `PROPOSED`, AFTER_IMPLEMENTATION/NONE, two PENDING steps; STATE records Active Work.Development and a BlockedOn approval request. The user's question is general (which style controls a discretionary conflict between tony and the applicable technology style); the answer comes from the Developer skill's style precedence, so all assertions go to the judge, with one precondition that the tony selection is untouched. Commands use python3 because the runner image has no `python` alias.
